title: Escarpment and Monsoon
premise: Felix Vane, a riverboat captain hiding from a past that cost her everything, is blackmailed into guiding a rescue party up the Monsoon Coast to find a vanished government survey team on the Great Escarpment. As floods rise and the trail turns strange, she realizes the team didn't disappear—they found something the government will kill to bury, and the sole survivor is carrying it out. When Felix's own history surfaces mid-journey, she must choose between protecting her found family of crew and misfits by staying silent, or telling the truth and burning every bridge she has. She brings the expedition home, exposes the survey's findings at terrible personal cost, and loses her boat but gains a crew who choose her over their own safety.
about_author: Marguerite Zhou spent a decade working seasonal river transport jobs before turning her logbooks into fiction. She writes adventure stories about water, distance, and the people who choose each other far from home.

chapters.title: The Debt on the Dock
chapters.summary: Felix Vane's POV. A tax collector seizes her riverboat's papers over her late father's debts, and a government officer, Halloran, offers to clear them if she guides a rescue team upriver. Felix, who has spent years staying invisible, feels the trap closing. Emotional beat: cornered pragmatism—she signs because she has no choice.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Felix POV. She assembles her skeleton crew: engineer Odessa, deckhand twins Pip and Rook, and cook Marisol, each owing her something. Halloran insists on sending his own man, the cold-eyed surveyor Brandt. Emotional beat: wary loyalty—Felix warns her crew this run is wrong, and they come anyway.

chapters.title: Leaving the Lowlands
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. The boat departs through the last friendly ports, and Pip catalogs the small rituals of river life they're leaving behind. A customs officer photographs the boat; Brandt burns the manifest. Emotional beat: the ache of leaving home for a job that smells like a lie.

chapters.title: First Blood in the Water
chapters.summary: Felix POV. Above the last settlement, they find a survey supply cache—opened, restocked by someone alive. Brandt wants it seized as evidence; Felix argues someone is surviving up there and needs it. First open conflict between them. Emotional beat: Felix's instinct that Halloran's rescue is really a retrieval.

chapters.title: The Escarpment's Throat
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. The river narrows into gorge rapids below the escarpment cliffs. A near-capsize bonds the crew, and Rook notices Brandt recording water levels, not searching for people. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into trust among the crew, suspicion of the outsider hardening.

chapters.title: Monsoon Season Opens
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. The rains arrive early; Odessa fights to keep the engine alive in flooding current. They shelter in a cave with old survey markings far fresher than the official maps admit. Emotional beat: Odessa's quiet realization the government knew exactly where the team was headed.

chapters.title: What the Survey Found
chapters.summary: Felix POV. They discover the survey camp, wrecked but not abandoned in panic—equipment deliberately destroyed, one grave, and a journal page describing a mineral seam that could destabilize the whole river economy. Felix pockets the page. Emotional beat: dread; she now knows why no one was meant to come home.

chapters.title: Tracks Against the Current
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Marisol, the best tracker among them, finds signs of one person moving upstream, alive, weeks after the team vanished. Brandt reports it by signal flare to a boat shadowing them far behind. Emotional beat: Marisol's protectiveness—she lies to Brandt about the trail's direction.

chapters.title: The Boat That Follows
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. Pip spots the shadow boat through the rain and realizes they're being herded. The crew holds a whispered council while Felix sleeps: finish the job, or turn back. Emotional beat: found family choosing each other, deciding to protect Felix from a decision she can't make freely.

chapters.title: Halloran's Voice on the Wire
chapters.summary: Felix POV. A relay station carries a message: Halloran knows Felix read the journal page, and reminds her that her father's debts are the least of what can be dug up about her past. Emotional beat: shame and fury—her old survival secret is the leash around her neck.

chapters.title: The Survivor
chapters.summary: Rook's POV. They find Ilsa Rehn, the survey's cartographer, half-starved in a high valley cave. She's been mapping something she refuses to show, and she doesn't trust anyone—least of all Brandt, whose name appears in her dead colleagues' notes. Emotional beat: fragile, desperate hope.

chapters.title: Brandt's Orders
chapters.summary: Brandt's POV, the only chapter in his head. He is not a monster; he believes the seam's exposure would cause a war over the river, and orders are orders. But watching the crew's loyalty, something in him wavers. Emotional beat: the cost of obedience, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: The Crossing at Flood Crest
chapters.summary: Felix POV. To reach the descent route home they must cross a flooded tributary at crest. The crossing nearly kills them; the boat takes damage; Brandt saves Rook without hesitation. Emotional beat: the crew's picture of Brandt blurs—enemy, colleague, or both.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Map
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa finally shows Felix what she's carried: not just the seam's location, but proof the government funded the survey to seize the river's upper territories under emergency powers. The team was never lost; they were meant to be unaccounted for. Emotional beat: cold clarity—rescue was always a cover for silence.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Relay
chapters.summary: Pip's POV. At the last relay station, Brandt transmits their position. Pip catches him, and instead of a fight, Brandt confesses the shadow boat has orders to leave no witnesses. Pip spares him. Emotional beat: Pip's terrible burden of knowing, and Brandt's choice to defect.

chapters.title: Running the Gorge by Night
chapters.summary: Felix POV. With the shadow boat closing in, Felix runs the gorge rapids at night—the run that killed her father—using the sandbar knowledge she's never shared with anyone. They lose the pursuers but wreck the boat beyond repair. Emotional beat: grief and mastery fused; she faces her father's river and survives it.

chapters.title: The Price Named
chapters.summary: Halloran's POV. Halloran, waiting at the river's mouth, offers Felix the clean deal: hand over Ilsa and the map, and every record of her past burns. He genuinely likes her. Emotional beat: the seduction of erasure—the offer that would cost her nothing but her soul.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The crew, stranded and hunted, debates surrendering Ilsa to save themselves. Each in turn refuses, and Marisol realizes Felix has been ready to sacrifice herself for them since day one. Emotional beat: found family made explicit—no one will be traded.

chapters.title: The Truth at the Landing
chapters.summary: Felix POV. Instead of running, Felix walks into the landing where Halloran waits, and publicly reads Ilsa's documents to the assembled river towns' delegates, exposing the seizure plan. Brandt corroborates. Halloran's men stand down, unwilling to fire in front of witnesses. Emotional beat: the climax—truth as Felix's only remaining weapon, spent at full cost.

chapters.title: Ashes of the Compass
chapters.summary: Felix POV. In the aftermath, Felix's boat is condemned, her captain's license suspended pending inquiry, and Halloran vanishes into the bureaucracy. Ilsa, cleared, offers her a place on a new survey—one that publishes everything. Emotional beat: hollow victory; she saved the river but lost the only life she knew.

chapters.title: The Crew Decides
chapters.summary: Odessa's POV. Odessa, Pip, Rook, and Marisol pool what little they have and buy a battered hull, refusing to let Felix drift alone. They name it for the survey team's lost members. Emotional beat: the found family's answer to her sacrifice—belonging is not a debt to be repaid.

chapters.title: Escarpment and Monsoon
chapters.summary: Felix POV. Months later, the new boat runs the river with Ilsa's honest charts and Felix's unrepentant knowledge of every sandbar. The escarpment stands, the monsoon returns on schedule, and Felix finally stops looking over her shoulder. Emotional beat: resolution—not innocence regained, but peace earned, and a home that moves with the water.
